title: Bayesian ablation notes and mini-trials
content:
Purpose: quick personal ledger for small-scale Bayesian ablation runs — capture priors, quantization, perf numbers, and immediate takeaways. Not an official experiment record; meant as a scratchpad before formalizing into the eval harness.

Summary notes:
- Trying a tiny ablation sweep of prior choices (Gaussian vs Student-t vs narrow Gaussian) + low-precision quant variants to see quality vs latency/cost tradeoffs on the small RAG prompt batch.
- All runs used same seed set (5 seeds), same eval prompts (dev-1k subset), no KV/prefix cache to isolate per-token throughput.
- Primary interest: whether heavier tails (Student-t) reduce hallucination for the few-shot prompts and how that interacts with quantization.

Mini results table (compact):
Trial | Prior | LR | Quant | Batch | Tokens/s | Median latency (ms) | Cost /1k tok | Dev RougeL
T-A1 | N(0,1)      | 1e-4 | int8  | 8  | 220  | 85  | $0.012 | 0.430
T-A2 | StudentT(df=3) | 1e-4 | int8  | 8  | 210  | 92  | $0.013 | 0.455
T-B1 | N(0,0.5)    | 5e-5 | int4  | 16 | 250  | 78  | $0.009 | 0.412
T-B2 | StudentT(df=5) | 5e-5 | int4  | 16 | 240  | 83  | $0.010 | 0.438
T-C1 | N(0,1) + temp anneal | 2e-4 | int8 | 8 | 215 | 88 | $0.0125 | 0.437

Quick observations:
- StudentT priors (T-A2, T-B2) gave higher RougeL on dev subset consistently across seeds (+0.02–0.03) relative to matching Gaussian runs.
- int4 quant yields ~20% lower cost and slightly better tokens/s (B1 vs A1), but variance between seeds is higher (occasional outlier bursts in latency).
- Performance hit for StudentT appears to be ~6–8 ms median latency in these configs; still within acceptable SLO but worth tracking tail percentiles.
- LR interaction: the narrower Gaussian (N(0,0.5)) benefits from lower LR; higher LR produced unstable losses for narrow priors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Run T-A2 with batch=16 (same tokens) to see if latency tradeoff changes; hypothesis: batching will mask CPU-side quant decode overhead and reduce observed latency gap.
- Add a posterior predictive check pass: sample 200 prompts, manually label hallucinations/critical errors (low-effort check).
- Reproduce best config (T-B2) with KV cache enabled — need to ensure caching doesn't change qual metrics (it should only improve throughput).
- Check 99th percentile latency for T-A2 on dedicated infra (non-shared GPU) — previous runs were on shared dev pool.

Run commands / quick notes:
- runner: infra/mini-runner v0.9 (local docker image), script: experiments/mini_ablation/run.sh --trial T-A2 --seeds 5 --no-cache
- perf capture: use /tools/latency-capture --prometheus=true --label=jasper-mini-2024-08

Slack refs / links:
- quick thread: slack://channels/eng-applied-ml/thread/CK9AB12 (notes from Aisha on seed variance)
- PR with int4 kernels: github:infra/model-ops#987 (linked above)

Next actions (ordered):
1) Run T-A2 batch=16 (Jasper) — target window: 1h, tag run with "bayes-ablation-aug1".
2) Posterior predictive quick-labeling (Aisha & Jasper) — 200 samples, simple 0/1 hallucination tag.
3) Collate seed variance into small boxplot and push to confluence if signal strong.
4) If StudentT gains hold, propose a small canary to serve StudentT-prior model variant behind A/B (check cost delta).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep this file lean; move results and seed-level CSVs into shareable drive folder once we've validated repeats.
- If variance is high, bump number of seeds to 10 for final check before any rollout discussion.
- Document exact quant bits and kernel version when moving to dedicated run (kernel changes matter).

End of scratchpad (will formalize after runs).
